title: Build TimeDelta from integer microseconds when deserializing
description: TimeDelta._deserialize passed a float in the precision unit straight to timedelta(), which does its own per-unit float arithmetic and can drift for large values. This converts to whole microseconds first, mirroring how _serialize already works through microseconds. Adds a test that large week/hour counts come back exact.

bugs.description: int() truncates toward zero, while timedelta() rounds to the nearest microsecond (as the class docstring documents: '1.1234567' seconds -> 123457 microseconds). With this PR it becomes 123456, and sub-microsecond inputs such as 0.0009 ms become 0 instead of 1. Negative values are also biased toward zero. Fix: round(value * microseconds_per_unit).
